text:
kevin: quick update — ran the p95-driven batching experiment this morning against prod-like load for routes: /chat:standard, /chat:premium, /embed. focused on dynamic token_budget per request based on route tier + KV cache hit_prob.

maria: nice. numbers?

kevin: baseline (current heuristic): static token_budget=256
- /chat:standard p95=210ms
- /chat:premium p95=190ms
- /embed p95=170ms

kevin: new heuristic: dynamic token_budget = clamp(route_target_tokens * (1 + 0.5*cache_miss_rate), min=64, max=512)
- /chat:standard p95=165ms (-45ms)
- /chat:premium p95=160ms (-30ms)
- /embed p95=168ms (~)

tess: wow standard improved a lot. what's the batch size distribution look like?

kevin: median batch_len up ~12 -> lower kernel invocation overhead. tail batches slightly longer; important note: when KV cache_miss spikes, our batch builder increases token_budget which sometimes produces larger batches that push single-GPU kernel selection to attention-optimized kernels — some models then picked different CUDA kernels and we saw a 3-4% throughput regression on fp16 path.

jules: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious about kernel timings.

kevin: here — profiler excerpt (simplified):
```
Kernel: attn_cuBlas    time=1.6ms -> 2.0ms (+25%)
Kernel: fused_ffn     time=0.9ms -> 0.95ms (+5%)
KV cache lookup    0.12ms (unchanged)
Batch merge overhead 0.04ms -> 0.06ms
```

kevin: regression happens specifically when batch_token_count > 1024 and sequence_len > 512 — kernel selector switched to an alternate cuBLAS path that has worse latency for short sequences but better throughput for huge batches.

sam: so p95 win came from fewer kernel launches but we flipped to a slower kernel in the big batch tail. how often do we hit that tail in production?

kevin: tail frequency low (~2% of requests) but they dominate p99; for p95 effect is positive because median improved; still we want deterministic SLO behavior per route.

maria: can we bias queue policy to limit max_batch_tokens for premium routes so they never trigger that kernel? e.g. cap at 900 tokens for premium, allow standard to use up to 1400?

kevin: yeah proposal: per-route token_budget_target array by tier + adaptive backoff when kernel_selector maps to high-latency path. Pseudocode:
```
if route == premium: max_batch_tokens = 900
elif route == standard: max_batch_tokens = min(1400, avg_queue_tokens*1.2)
if kernel_selector.estimate(latency) > route_p95_target: reduce target *= 0.85
```

tess: we should also incorporate KV hit_ratio per model shard — high hit_ratio => can tolerate larger batch tokens because actual compute per request lower (less kv loads) correct?

kevin: yes. saw that in profiling: cache_hit_rate>0.8 reduced per-token compute 18%. so token_budget should be multiplied by (1 + alpha*(1 - hit_rate)) where alpha≈0.5.

jules: for rollout we need canary config + automated rollback if p95 increases >5% vs baseline. also add kernel-level telemetry (kernel_id, batch_tokens, seq_len) to perf logs.

infra-bot: deploy hook queued: canary config created as redwood/batching/p95-dyn/2026-01-25

sam: one more: queue policy — prefer age-based vs size-based when approaching p95 window. If request.age > 10ms, flush even if batch small. That helped p95 in earlier experiments.

kevin: good point. current builder waits up to 15ms or tokens threshold. lower the max_wait_ms to 10ms for premium route only.

maria: next steps?

kevin: action items:
- jules: add kernel-level telemetry + metric -> due EOD
- tess: update canary config with per-route caps and max_wait_ms -> PR by tomorrow
- sam: run larger scale perf job to validate tail (24h) -> start tonight
- infra: schedule canary rollout 10:30 UTC

maria: if we see regression on canary, rollback + revert commit 72f9d (recent kernel selector change) — that one correlates with the alternate path.

kevin: agreed. also plan to add a small kernel_selector shim: if estimated_latency_for(kernel_id) > route_threshold then fallback to alternative kernel (even if less throughput) for p95-critical routes.

tess: 👍 will follow up in PR comments

kevin: thanks all. saving experiment logs to S3: s3://redwood-perf/p95-dyn/1763501234/ — includes full profiler and batch traces. ping me if you want access.

maria: looked through logs quickly — one odd trace where cache_miss rate jumped during a model reload window; keep an eye on that.

kevin: noted. end of thread.
